meta.title: Who really said "There is only one boss. The customer. And he can fire everybody in the company from the chairman on down, simply by spending his money somewhere else"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: The idea is Walton’s — his memoir says “the customer is our boss.” This polished sentence is not in it, and no source for the wording has been found.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'There is only one boss. The customer. And he can fire everybody in the company from the chairman on down, simply by spending his money somewhere else'?
meta.ogDescription: Walton’s idea, in words nobody can source to him — his memoir says it quite differently.

answer.label: Walton’s idea — but not Walton’s words
answer.sourceLine: The thought is genuinely his: Sam Walton: Made in America has him writing that “everything we’ve done since we started Wal-Mart has been devoted to this idea that the customer is our boss.” But this polished version — only one boss, fire everybody from the chairman on down — is not in the book, whose complete text we searched, and no one who repeats it names a source. Who sharpened it into this sentence, we could not establish.

source.heading: Where it actually comes from

docMeta.dd: “…this idea that the customer is our boss.”
Not in the book — complete text searched

source.excerpt:
DAVID GLASS: “…On the other hand it’s simple. If the customers are the bosses, all you have to do is please them.”

I couldn’t agree with David more. Everything we’ve done since we started Wal-Mart has been devoted to this idea that the customer is our boss.
trail: We searched the complete text of Walton’s memoir, Sam Walton: Made in America (Doubleday, June 1992), in the Bantam printing whose own front matter states that it “contains the complete text of the original hardcover edition” and that “not one word has been omitted”. The copy catalogued at the Internet Archive ↗ is lending-restricted and cannot be searched from its catalogue page; the text we read is the Archive’s separately held full-text scan of that same printing, item made-in-america-sam-walton, so the search can be repeated. The phrases “only one boss”, “fire everybody”, “fire everyone” and “somewhere else” return nothing in it.

What the book does contain, in Walton’s own voice: “Everything we’ve done since we started Wal-Mart has been devoted to this idea that the customer is our boss.” It follows a quoted passage from David Glass ending “If the customers are the bosses, all you have to do is please them.” The idea is documented; this wording is not.
His own numbered rules make the same point in his own register — Rule 8 reads “EXCEED your customers’ expectations”, not anything about firing a chairman.
Wikiquote’s Sam Walton page ↗ does not carry this sentence at all, and Quote Investigator has no article on it.
source.excerptNote: This is the closest thing in Walton’s own book to the famous sentence: a set-off passage from Walmart chief executive David Glass, followed by Walton agreeing in his own voice. Neither man says “there is only one boss”, and neither mentions firing anybody.

author.name: Sam Walton
author.heading: About Sam Walton
author.metaLine: 1918–1992 · American retailer, founder of Walmart and Sam’s Club
author.bio: Samuel Moore Walton (29 March 1918 – 5 April 1992) bought a Ben Franklin variety store in Newport, Arkansas in 1945 and opened the first Wal-Mart Discount City in Rogers, Arkansas in 1962; Sam’s Club followed in 1983. From 1982 to 1988 he was the richest person in the United States, and he received the Presidential Medal of Freedom. He told his own story once, in Sam Walton: Made in America (1992), written with John Huey and published weeks before his death.

misattribution.heading: Often misattributed
misattribution.intro: This is the right person and the wrong words — the most common shape a famous quotation takes, and the hardest to spot, because the sentiment checks out.

items.why: He really did build the company on it and really did write it down: “Everything we’ve done since we started Wal-Mart has been devoted to this idea that the customer is our boss.” Nobody should walk away thinking the sentiment was invented for him.
Not in the memoir, not on Wikiquote ↗, and not traced by anyone who repeats it. Somebody tightened Walton’s idea into an aphorism and his name stayed attached; we could not find out who, or when.

items.who: His memoir, Sam Walton: Made in America
items.why: Frequently given as the source. We searched the book’s complete text: the phrase “only one boss” does not occur in it, and neither does any form of “fire everybody”.

misattribution.truthLine: Walton’s version is plainer and it is his: the customer is our boss. The chairman, the firing and the money spent somewhere else are somebody else’s embroidery.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Walton meant the idea structurally, not as a slogan. The memoir passage sits inside an argument about thinking like a customer down to the placement of stock on a shelf, and it is introduced by his chief executive, David Glass, describing managers walking a department manager through her own aisle asking what a customer would want.

The aphorism that travels under his name keeps the hierarchy and adds a threat — the customer can fire you, from the chairman down. That is a sharper, more quotable thought than the one in the book, which is probably why it displaced it.
detailsBody: Walton’s own numbered rules run in the same plain register: Rule 8 is “EXCEED your customers’ expectations. If you do, they’ll come back over and over.” He had a house style, and this sentence is not in it.

What we could not establish: who first put the line in this form. We found no dated printing early enough to trace, and the sites carrying it give no citations, so the point at which Walton’s idea became this sentence is still open.

sourcesVerified.claim: Wikiquote's Sam Walton page does not carry "There is only one boss. The customer..." — it holds a single, different quotation.
Wikipedia confirms Sam Walton (1918–1992) founded Walmart in 1962 and Sam's Club in 1983.

The Internet Archive catalogues "Sam Walton, made in America: my story" (Walton, Sam, 1918-1992). The copy held there is lending-restricted — it offers Borrow only — so the book's text cannot be searched from that page.

A full-text scan of the same Bantam printing of Sam Walton, Made in America, held at the Internet Archive as item "made-in-america-sam-walton", contains no occurrence of "only one boss", "fire everybody", "fire everyone" or "somewhere else". It does contain a set-off passage labelled "DAVID GLASS" ending "If the customers are the bosses, all you have to do is please them.", followed by Walton writing "I couldn't agree with David more. Everything we've done since we started Wal-Mart has been devoted to this idea that the customer is our boss."; Rule 8 reading "EXCEED your customers' expectations. If you do, they'll come back over and over."; and elsewhere the label "DAVID GLASS, CEO, WAL-MART".
